summary.what_it_does: The page is a directory of privacy tools organised by category (network, browser, search, files, messaging, accounts, devices, developer). Users pick an app they currently use and are shown private alternatives, and there is a separate section of European-based alternatives. It includes an "Editor's Top Picks | 2026" list of twelve tools, a trending list of open-source privacy projects pulled from GitHub, and FAQ-style guidance on encryption, VPNs, incognito mode and open-source trust. Several listed entries are marked as paid advertisements and are not part of the editorial recommendations.
notable: Editor's top picks and a European alternatives section
Recommends tools by category and states its selection criteria (open source, independent audits, track record)
Listed as an external link in awesome-selfhosted
caveats: Contains paid advertisements mixed among the listings, including VPNs and data-removal services
Recommendations are editorial opinions; the page itself does not list prices for most tools
Some listed tools (e.g. Bitwarden) are free only for personal use, per the page
